title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes Grothendieck tries to axiomatize a 'structure de contrôle' for tame topology. The data are a set L of 'lieux' together with certain sets of parts of L called 'figures'. The members of a figure are its strict opens ('ouverts stricts'), which play the role of cells or strata. Two figures are 'compatible' when, roughly, their union is again a figure. A family of figures that is pairwise compatible in this way is a 'configuration'.

Previous page. Conj 4 says compatibility of F and G is tested on multiplets. The corollary says a family (F_i) is a configuration iff all cross-pairs of multiplets are compatible; for finite I the union is then a figure with the F_i as subfigures. This is a 'pairwise determines all' (flag-type) axiom. He also introduced 'point-based' (set-theoretic, 'ensembliste') structures, in which ensemblistically compatible figures are automatically compatible.

This page.
(1) Scope. He notes that for non-set-theoretic structures this point-based reduction should probably be dropped, to be checked on the non-ensemblist examples still to come.
(2) A proposed condition, marked '(?)' and flagged in the margin 'à reformuler': two figures F, G are compatible iff
  - they are ensemblistically compatible, and
  - for strict opens U of F and V of G with U ≠ V, and all x ∈ U, y ∈ V, the pair {{x},{y}} is a figure.
(3) Notation. For x ∈ L, F_x := {{x}} is the figure concentrated at the single point x. 'F_x, F_y compatible' means {F_x, F_y} is a figure; this always holds when x = y.
(4) Points x, y are 'disjoint' if they are distinct and compatible; the 2-element set {x,y} ∈ P_2(L) is then a distinguished pair for C (word uncertain).
(5) Parts A, B ⊂ L are 'C-disjoint' if every x ∈ A and y ∈ B are disjoint, which forces A ∩ B = ∅.

Next page. The condition is restated: F, G compatible iff for all strict opens U of F and V of G, either U = V or U, V are C-disjoint. So in the point-based case the whole compatibility structure reduces to one symmetric irreflexive relation on L ('disjointness'), a graph. Figures/configurations become clique-like objects of that graph.

Aftermath. On 12 June he finds, from the combinatorics of topological pseudo-discs, that lieux and figures alone are insufficient: extra 'order/equivalence' data tied to the boundary ∂D is needed. The framework being set up here is thus about to be put in question.
errors: Internal tension: the page condition allows overlapping U ≠ V (x = y is trivially compatible). The next-page reformulation ('U = V or U, V C-disjoint') forbids any overlap of distinct strict opens, because C-disjointness requires the points to be distinct. The two versions agree only if distinct strict opens are already assumed disjoint (e.g. via ensemblist compatibility).
Grothendieck himself marks the condition '(?)' and 'à reformuler', and restricts it to set-theoretic ('ensembliste') structures pending examples; it is a tentative axiom, not a result.

ideas.what: Point figures F_x = {{x}}, and reduction of compatibility of figures to a binary 'disjointness' relation on points
ideas.modern_name: symmetric (in)compatibility relation / graph on a ground set; configurations as cliques (flag-complex or coherence-space type structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: coherence spaces: Girard (1986-87); flag/clique complexes: standard combinatorics
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) calls for 'topologie modérée' but contains no such axiomatics

ideas.what: C-disjoint parts: A, B with all cross pairs of points disjoint
ideas.modern_name: independent/separated sets relative to a relation

ideas.what: Attempt to axiomatize tame topology ('structure de contrôle') via lieux plus families of parts ('figures') with a compatibility relation
ideas.modern_name: closest: o-minimal structures / stratified spaces / cell-complex axiomatics
ideas.where_published: Only the programmatic call in Esquisse d'un programme §5

missed.claim: In the point-based ('ensembliste') case, the whole compatibility structure of figures and configurations is determined by one symmetric relation on lieux, with configurations given by a pairwise (flag) condition. Structurally this is a coherence space/clique complex inside an attempted foundation of tame topology. It was written in 1986, contemporaneous with Girard's coherence spaces, with no link between the two.
missed.quote: On dit que x, y sont "disjoints" s'ils sont distincts et compatibles ... Deux parties A, B de L sont dites disjointes (... C-disjointes) si ∀x∈A, ∀y∈B, x, y sont disjoints
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck's tame-topology axiomatics briefly reducing to graph/clique combinatorics, a route he himself abandoned two days later (pseudo-disc obstruction). No mathematically new result.

missed.claim: Whether non-set-theoretic control structures admit a point-free version of the compatibility criterion is left open ('à vérifier sur les exemples non ensemblistes à venir').
missed.quote: Pour les structures non ensemblistes, il y a lieu de supprimer ceci (à vérifier sur les exemples non ensemblistes à venir)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal; superseded by his own realization (12 June) that figures need extra ordering data near the boundary.

deep.surprise_reason: Tentative definitional bookkeeping (point figures, disjoint points, C-disjoint sets) within an abandoned axiomatization of tame topology. It is historically interesting as a snapshot of the 1986 'Analysis situs' attempt, but contains no substantive result; the coherence-space resemblance is structural and elementary.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, 'C' in 'F, C' and 'U et C' should be read 'G': the condition concerns two figures F, G, and strict opens U of F and V of G.
'deux [-...-] ouverts [-...-] de F' is likely 'deux ouverts stricts U de F, V de G'.
'Cond 1' / '(?) Cond' is likely 'Cond' or 'Conj' and refers back to Conj 4; margin reads 'à reformuler (cond. 4?)'.
'C-option' is doubtful; perhaps 'C-paire' or a similar term for a distinguished 2-element subset.
'(ou mieux [?] le C contraire [?] C - ou C-disjointes)' probably reads something like '(ou mieux, quand on veut préciser C, C-disjointes)'.
'convenant en le seul point x' is plausibly 'concentrée en le seul point x'.
